The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,1)$ and the line segment for $x\in (1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,= & {\int }_{-3}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+{\int }_{1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ {\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,= & \,{{{\int }_{-3}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}\,+\,{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,1).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\,bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\,bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 4 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x\, & =\,{A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\,8+6 \\  & =\,14.\end{aligned}
$$
